text:
Vanessa Ortiz: heads up on Shadow Traffic beta ramp — we need to capacity-plan the extra GPU load from sampling. Right now fleet is sized for primary inference + headroom, but shadow adds a *second* decode path and tends to show up as “mystery” utilization unless we cap it hard by tier + region.

Vanessa Ortiz: proposing we ship with (1) per-tier global shadow budgets, and (2) per-region caps so we don’t blow out eu-central during a launch. Need input from autoscaling/quotas/SRE.

Keiko Yamamoto: +1. also want to avoid shadow runner competing with primary for the same pools. if we can, route shadow to “overflow” pools or at least enforce strict queue + token budget so it sheds load first.

Cole Summers: from quotas side we can model it as “shadow_gpu_seconds” budget (or shadow_tokens) per customer + per org tier. enforcement point could be: gateway admission (cheap) + shadow-runner queue (authoritative). anyone already plumbing meter tags for shadow?

Emily Zhao: data-plane note: shadow runner uses same model runtime path but async worker. right now it can hit the same cluster unless we set pool constraints in policy. we *do* have backpressure in PR-48275 but defaults matter.

Sean Gallagher: SRE concern: any saturation event must fail *shadow only* and never impact primary p99. so caps should be conservative and enforced even if someone sets sampling=10% in a RoutePolicy.

Mina Haddad: routing can support per-route shadow policy, but for fleet we need global guardrails. suggestion: “effective_sampling = min(requested_sampling, tier_cap, region_cap, fleet_emergency_cap)”. emergency cap tied to kill switch.

Amara Diallo: gateway can do sampling, but enforcement at gateway alone isn’t enough because sampling % *times* traffic spikes can still overload shadow workers. recommend: gateway caps per-org + region, and shadow queue does token-bucket + drops.

InfraBot: Fleet snapshot (rolling 7d peak)
- us-east-1: 68% avg util, 82% p95, headroom ~18%
- us-west-2: 61% avg util, 77% p95, headroom ~23%
- eu-central-1: 74% avg util, 88% p95, headroom ~12%
- ap-southeast-1: 52% avg util, 69% p95, headroom ~31%

Vanessa Ortiz: eu-central headroom is the scary one. if we let enterprise shadow at 1% there during business hours we could tip it.

Vanessa Ortiz: rough math (sanity check): if primary decode cost is ~1.0x GPU-seconds per request, shadow is ~0.8–1.2x depending on max_tokens. so 1% sampling ~ ~1% extra GPU time *for those routes*, but concentrated on hot routes + regions.

Keiko Yamamoto: also batching differs. shadow runner likely sees less batching efficiency since it’s async + sampled (smaller batch sizes) → higher cost per token. so assume worse-than-linear impact.

Dylan Brooks: product expectation for beta: most accounts start at 0.1%–0.5% sampling, with ability to go up to 1% for specific routes while tuning. we need hard ceilings so PMs can say “safe by default”.

Cole Summers: proposal for *tier caps* (max requested sampling per org, aggregated across routes):
- Free/Dev: max 0% (off)
- Pro: max 0.1% global, max 0.25% per-route
- Enterprise: max 0.5% global, max 1.0% per-route
and also a *shadow compute budget* (e.g., 2% of primary spend) to prevent long-tail abuse.

Sean Gallagher: + add “burst” handling: allow brief exceed (like 2x for 60s) then clamp, or just hard drop? I’d rather hard drop shadow than create queue growth that causes noisy alerts.

Emily Zhao: shadow queue already supports drop-on-overflow with metric `shadow_eval.drop_count` and reason tags. we can configure max queue depth per region. hard drop is fine since this is eval-only.

Vanessa Ortiz: ok. for *regional caps* (cap of total fleet GPU utilization attributable to shadow), we can do:
- us-east-1: shadow <= 3% of total GPU time
- us-west-2: shadow <= 3%
- eu-central-1: shadow <= 1%
- ap-southeast-1: shadow <= 2%
implemented as “shadow_runner max concurrent tokens” or “max in-flight shadow requests” per region.

Keiko Yamamoto: makes sense. we can translate those into concurrency limits based on average shadow request profile per model (p50 tokens in/out). we should keep it model-agnostic initially: limit on “estimated_gpu_ms” emitted by runtime.

Mina Haddad: do we want *dedicated shadow pools* per region? even small (like 1-2% of GPUs) would isolate primary. downside is waste if no one uses shadow.

Vanessa Ortiz: for beta I’d avoid new pools — too slow to provision + operationally messy. prefer shared pools with strict limiter + preemption (shadow drops first). we can revisit dedicated pools post-beta if usage is steady.

Amara Diallo: to make shared pools safer, gateway should tag shadow requests with lower priority so scheduler can de-prioritize. if scheduler doesn’t support, at least shadow runner should back off when primary p99 degrades.

Sean Gallagher: +1 on guardrail: “shadow auto-throttle when primary SLO burn rate > threshold”. simplest signal: if primary queue depth / pending requests > X, shadow concurrency goes to 0 until recovered.

Cole Summers: ok but we need to be careful about circular dependencies (shadow metrics pipeline lag). use immediate infra signals (GPU util, primary queue depth) not judge outputs.

Keiko Yamamoto: action items I can take:
1) convert regional % caps into concrete concurrency/token limits per region (assume worst-case batching)
2) add autoscaler note: shadow runner does *not* trigger scale-up beyond region cap
3) add emergency cap config exposed to SRE (0 -> off)

Vanessa Ortiz: I’ll write this up for the beta checklist + share with Dylan/Marissa. 
Tentative decision (unless objections):
- Default sampling: Enterprise 0.1% per-route, Pro 0.0% (off)
- Hard max requested sampling: Pro 0.25%/route, Ent 1%/route
- Hard regional compute caps: us-east/us-west 3%, eu-central 1%, apse 2%
- Behavior on exceed: drop shadow immediately (no queue growth)

Dylan Brooks: works for me. pls include wording for Console UI copy: “Shadow runs may be dropped under load to protect primary traffic” so customers don’t interpret missing data as a bug.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: and please make sure alerts page on *shadow drop spikes* but not wake anyone unless primary impacted. we got burned by noisy paging last time.

Vanessa Ortiz: noted. will sync with SRE on alert thresholds. thanks all.
